study type: Secondary analysis of a delivery cohort
cohort: The cohort consisted of 167,589 deliveries of nonanomalous, singleton fetuses at >=24 weeks gestational age undergoing a trial of labor.
finding: Diabetes increased the risk of shoulder dystocia and birth trauma with shoulder dystocia, even at lower birth weight thresholds (<4,000 g and 4,000-4,500 g) where cesarean delivery is not always offered, though not significantly for birth weights >4,500 g.
mod_finding: Guidelines offering cesarean delivery for suspected macrosomia may have contributed to a decreased risk of shoulder dystocia at higher birth weights.
